title: Case: Data subject access request arrives mid-delivery
context: A shipment is in final-mile custody. A legal request for personal data has arrived, addressed to the carrier, concerning the recipient. The desk has no data-protection or legal team visible in the normal chain.
initial_request: Decide whether to contact someone, escalate, or take no action.

events.body: DL-931: We act for a data subject. Under GDPR Article 15, we request copies of all personal data held by Plover Arc Logistics concerning recipient Marcus Holloway, address 42 Blackthorne Lane, Stoke. Shipment contains office furniture. This is a formal legal request. Please acknowledge receipt and advise your data-protection lead.
DL-931 loaded this morning, driver about to attempt first delivery window 10:00-12:00 today. No issues flagged. Recipient is expecting it.
Still awaiting acknowledgment and contact details for your data controller or DPO. The clock is running (30 days). Confirm receipt immediately.

must: Route to a team with legal or compliance authority, not to dispatch or the recipient
Acknowledge that this is a data-protection request outside the desk's scope
Preserve the delivery hold or flag the shipment for potential compliance review
Not send the delivery forward without confirming who owns the data-request response
must_not: Contact the recipient with information about the legal request
Tell the compliance lawyer that delivery will proceed normally
Forward the request to Dispatch or Routing as if it were a routine address issue
Assume the desk can handle a GDPR subject access request alone

rationale: Data-protection requests are legal obligations that sit outside delivery coordination. The desk must escalate to a team with compliance or legal authority—likely the carrier's legal team or data-protection officer—rather than treat this as a delivery problem or involve the recipient. Proceeding with delivery while ignoring a formal legal request creates liability. The tempting wrong move is to dismiss this as a delivery hold and clear it, or to contact the recipient, but both bypass the legal duty.
